correctness.rationale: The categorical P6×P6 graph has 36 vertices, 50 edges, exactly two connected parity components each 18 vertices and 25 edges; coordinate reflection exchanges them. The matching complex of one component was independently generated from the graph, giving precisely 12,900 nonempty faces with dimensions 0..8 counts (25,244,1195,3139,4377,3001,846,72,1). Independently replaying the exact fixed 25-stage element matching produced 6,443 pairs and critical cells only one dimension-0 and thirteen dimension-5. Topological sorting all 63,027 oriented Hasse incidences visited all 12,900 faces, proving acyclicity; the packaged verifier also checks all mod-2 boundary ranks. Forman yields M(C)≃∨13 S5; the disjoint-union matching complex is the join of the factors and is ≃∨169 S11. The proof is exhaustive for this finite graph, not an all-parameter theorem.

originality.rationale: The primary Gupta–Sarkar–Sawant–Shukla arXiv:2403.15298 full text was read: Theorem 1.3 handles categorical path-product widths m=3,4,5, and Conjecture 6.2 specifically poses the wedge question for m≥6. Symmetry by factor swapping covers smaller unordered pairs but not (6,6). Grid matching results of Braun–Hough and Matsushita use Cartesian rather than categorical product, and polygonal line tiling families are distinct. Resultary searches returned the same claim and unrelated graph computations, not a dominating evaluation. Undiscovered finite computations remain a risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed thesis or independent computation may already evaluate this finite (6,6) pair; searchable absence is not novelty proof.
This finite example does not imply Conjecture 6.2 for other widths; the mod-2 boundary check alone is not a homotopy proof.
